messages.author: b4ad0d1eb08bc819
messages.subject: Predict
parts:
I have run the following code for a two factor model.

strict.fit <- cfa(cfa.model, data = data,
                  ordered = ordered,
                  std.lv = FALSE,
                  check.gradient = FALSE,
                  meanstructure = TRUE,
                  group = 'ubr', 
                  group.equal = c('loadings', 'intercepts', 'residuals')) 

I would like to merge the predicted latent factor scores back to my data set. However, when I run:

fscores <- predict(fit) 
or 
fscores <- lavPredict(fit, append.data =TRUE) 

I end up with two lists, one for each group. This is fine but when I try to make it a dataframe using 

as.data.frame(fscores) 

I get the following error:

Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE,  : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 316, 720

The differing number of rows correctly flags how many are in each of my groups. However, I need to be able to merge this back to the original data frame and in the correct order. How can this be done?

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Predict
parts: I think you could solve this problem with unlist() and then rbind() for the two sets of factor scores, then merge that back into your main data by the ID number. I use tidyverse, so I'd use one of the join() family.

On Fri, 7 Aug 2020 at 06:53, Patrick (Malone Quantitative) <mal...@malonequantitative.com> wrote:
I think you could solve this problem with unlist() and then rbind() for the two sets of factor scores, then merge that back into your main data by the ID number. I use tidyverse, so I'd use one of the join() family.

dplyr::bind_rows() does this in one step - it will take every element of a list and rbind() them.
